en_how: A greyscale temperature map (whiter is hotter) is first drawn in Canvas: a house and trees on a cold night, a walking person and dog, footprints that darken according to when they were planted, breath puffs that spread and cool, chimney smoke flattened by the wind, all slightly blurred; a WebGL shader reads this map, looks each temperature up in a false-colour palette (black-purple through orange-yellow to white), sweeps a front across to swap in a second palette when the wind rises, and uses a Sobel operator to lay a thin white edge on every temperature jump; Canvas adds the crosshair and temperature readouts.
